## Make a demo

Build a spec with the Python builders, or write the same JSON by hand.

``` python
from rupaka.spec import *
from rupaka.render import md
d = demo('sum', 'Add two numbers', ask='Predict the sum before you see it.', state=dict(a=2, b=3), derive=[expr('a + b', 'sum')],
         blocks=[gate('s', 'What is {a} + {b}?', [4, 5, 6], 'sum', why='Say why, in one line.', context='For a = {a} and b = {b}:'),
                 readout('{a} + {b} = {sum}', after='s'),
                 row(slider('a', 'a', 0, 9, 1, lock='s'), slider('b', 'b', 0, 9, 1, lock='s'))])
assert validate(d) == []
fence = md(d)
```

`validate(spec)` gives a list of errors. Each error is `path: sentence`,
and the sentence names the fix. An empty list means that the spec is
good. Fix each error and run
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
again. `plain_errors(spec)` gives each text that is not plain English
(ASD-STE100 at US grade 9).

`from rupaka.agent import catalog` and `print(catalog())` give every
block and fn with its purpose and props. The catalog is the full list.
This sheet is a summary.

A text takes `{key}` for a state value, `{key:2}` for a value rounded to
two decimal places, and `{row.name}` for a field of a row. A gate
`prompt` and a
[`caption`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#caption) also
take `**bold**`.

## The think rule

A demo in `predict` mode asks before it shows.
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
refuses a spec that breaks one of these rules:

- A `predict` demo has at least one
  [`gate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#gate).
- A block that shows a value which a gate’s answer depends on waits for
  that gate. Give the block `after='<gate id>'`, or name the derived
  keys in the gate’s `hides`.
- A gate whose answer a control changes has a `context` that names the
  inputs, for example `'For {a}:'`.
- A `learn` demo (an explainer) has no gate, and no block in it has
  `after` or `lock`.

The learner predicts, locks in with Cmd+Return, sees the result, then
moves the controls. Give each control that feeds the answer
`lock='<gate id>'`. A locked control does not move before the lock in.
End the
[`caption`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#caption) with
a new question that the learner answers with the controls.

## Derived values

`expr(formula, out)` computes one number. A formula has `+ - * / ^`,
parentheses, number state keys,
`sin cos tan exp log sqrt abs min max floor ceil round`, `pi` and `e`.
`sin`, `cos` and `tan` take radians. A formula has no `%`, no comparison
and no condition.
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
refuses each of them.

- Wrap an angle to one circle with `x - 360*floor(x/360)`.
- Pick a case with
  [`rules`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#rules) (the
  first row of a table that matches) or
  [`lookup`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#lookup) (a
  row of a table by key or position).
- `expr('x^2 + b*x', 'curve', over=dict(x=[-5, 5, 101]))` gives a series
  of points for
  [`plot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#plot).

A block with `step: n` shows from step `n` of an explainer that has the
state key `step`.

A [`choice`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#choice) with
`resets`, for example `{"tick": 0}`, sets those state keys back when the
pick changes. Use it when a control such as a step bar belongs to the
picked case.

## Sound

A `sound` block plays a sample-free `strike` only on a click of Play, or
W on that button. It never plays on mount, state change, gate restore or
reveal. Use `after` to wait for a gate. Opening that gate again stops
audio and disables Play. The visible text labels synthesis as an
approximation. Optional `ref: {url, title}` links to a real lesson or
recording; it never plays the link. Use
`voice: {kind: "strike", frequency: 138.59, decay: 1.2, gain: 0.6, partials: [{ratio: 1, gain: 1}], noise: 0.08}`.
Frequency is 20–8000 Hz, decay is 0.01–5 seconds, and gains and noise
are 0–1. Use one to eight partials with ratio 0.0025–400 and gain 0–1.
Each partial stays at 20–8000 Hz. Optional `bend` is -1200–1200 cents;
the bent frequency must also stay in range. Voice fields cannot contain
URLs, samples or code. `tone` is reserved for later, not supported. See
`examples()['sound']` for the sourced Nam and Tha comparison.

A spec can embed profiles:
`profiles: {alias: {id, revision, school, data}}`, with `revision` equal
to `profile_hash(data)`. Check `data` with
[`profile_errors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#profile_errors).
A clean result means good structure and attribution, not true facts. A
sound has `voice` or `play: {profile, technique}`, never both. A `play`
technique with no voice shows its facts and sources, and Play stays
disabled. A sound with `play` shows the parts, facts and source links of
its technique when the block shows. A fact with no `school` shows for
all schools. A per-school fact shows only for the embed `school`. With
no fact for that school, the value shows as unknown. A gate names a
technique that gives its answer away in `hides`:
`profiles.<alias>.techniques.<id>`. Then each sound that plays it must
wait for that gate. This is a declared guard, not a detector: a sound
that no gate names can play before any gate. The raw spec is in the
page, so a hidden block is not a secret. See
`gallery()['mridangam-profile']`.

A profile can hold
`media: {id: {kind, src, credit, start, end, alt, sources}}`. `kind` is
`audio`, `image` or `video`. `credit` is `{who, license, url}`; the page
shows the link and never loads it. `src` is `asset:<sha256>.<ext>`, a
file that the host serves, or `youtube:<11-character id>` for a video
with `start` and `end`, at most 120 seconds apart. No other URL is
allowed. An image needs `alt`. A technique lists
`media: [{media, school}]`, with the same school rule as facts. A
technique voice can be `{kind: "sample", media: <audio id>}`. The media
of a technique shows only while its sound block shows, so a gate that
hides the technique also hides its media. A YouTube clip loads only when
the learner clicks Load video. The page loads an asset from
`data-rk-media` and the asset name (default `media/`).
`save(spec, path, media=folder)` copies the assets to `media/` beside
the page. In a notebook, `show(spec, assets=folder)` puts the assets in
the page as data URIs, up to `cap` bytes (default 4,000,000).
`rupaka.media` makes assets:
[`import_asset`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#import_asset),
[`clip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#clip) and
[`still`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#still) (with
ffmpeg), and
[`find_span`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/media.html#find_span)
for a phrase in a transcript. See `gallery()['mridangam-real']`.

## Rhythm

A `rhythm` block is a practice round:
`{type: "rhythm", profile: alias, pattern: [technique ids or "rest"], beats: "beats"}`.
It plays only when the learner clicks Start, or W on that button. Stop,
or W again, ends the round at once. The round is a count-in of
`count_in` short clicks (0–8, default 4), then the pattern `cycles`
times (1–16, default 2). One item of `pattern` is one beat. With `turns`
(default true), a silent Your turn cycle of the same length follows each
played cycle. The learner plays in that cycle. A quiet click on its
beats is off until the learner turns it on. `tempo` is 30–240 beats per
minute (default 60). The learner changes it with the slider, or A and D;
a change starts at the next cycle. Each stroke plays the voice of its
technique. A strike is synthesised. A technique in `pattern` must have a
voice. A sample plays its recording from the page or from a
`data-rk-media` base on the page’s own origin.
`show(spec, assets=folder)` puts the recording in the page. The rhythm
never loads a recording from another origin. When a recording does not
load, its strokes are silent and the block says so. `beats` names a list
in `state`. When a silent cycle is scheduled, the round writes there the
times of its beats, in seconds on the shared audio clock `ctx.audio()`.
A gate that hides a technique of the pattern makes the rhythm wait for
it, as for a sound. See `gallery()['mridangam-rhythm']`.

## Listen

A `listen` block times the learner’s drum strokes with the microphone,
on the device. It opens the microphone only on a click of Listen on this
device (W), and Stop listening (S) stops it. `beats: [key]` names the
`beats` key of a rhythm block in the same spec. That round writes the
beat times there, in seconds on the page audio clock.
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
refuses a listen block without a matching rhythm block. When that key
changes and its last beat has passed, the block writes
`[{beat, verdict, ms}]` to `out: [key]` and shows a line for each beat:
on, early N ms, late N ms or missed. `tolerance` (10–80 ms, default 30)
is on time; `window` (50–300 ms, default 150) is how far either side the
block looks for a stroke. `calibrate: false` hides the Calibrate step
(E), which plays 8 clicks and keeps the median delay of the taps. While
the microphone is on, a level meter and a count (Heard 7 strokes) show
that the block hears the drum, before any round. Keep my playing (Q) is
a box, off at first. When it is on, the block keeps the audio of the
last round only, from its first beat minus `window` to its last beat
plus `window` (at most 60 s), in page memory. After the round, Play what
I played (A) plays it on `ctx.audio()`, with a soft click on each beat
if Click on each beat (1) is on, and a timeline shows the beats and the
strokes heard. Save my playing (D) writes the round as a 16-bit WAV file
on the device. Stop listening, a tick off, the next round and leaving
the page drop the audio. `keep: false` leaves the box out. With the box
off, the block keeps no audio. It sends nothing. It needs a served page
with `listen-worklet.js` beside `rupaka.js`: in
[`page()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#page),
[`show()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#show),
[`md()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#md) and
[`save()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#save) it
says that the microphone is not available. See `examples()['listen']`.

## 3D scenes

``` python
s = demo('lift', 'Twice the weight', state=dict(step=1, cam='wide', w=4), derive=[expr('w * 2', 'up')],
         blocks=[gate('g', 'What is twice {w}?', [6, 8], 'up'),
                 scene(body('base', 'box', [2, 1, 2]), force([0, 1, 0], 'up', on='base', at=[0, 1.5, 0], label='lift, {up}', after='g'),
                       shot(bind='cam'), shot('close:base', step=2), bind='step', steps=['A box.', 'Look closer.'])])
assert validate(s) == []
```

- A [`scene`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#scene)
  holds only
  [`body`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#body),
  [`force`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#force),
  [`label3d`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#label3d)
  and [`shot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#shot)
  blocks. With `bind='step'` and `steps`, it builds one step at a time.
  A part with `step: n` shows from step `n`.
- The frame has `y` up. `at` is a place in the frame of the parent body.
  `rot` is a turn in degrees about `x`, `y` and `z`, and each item can
  be a state key. A positive turn about `y` moves `+x` toward `-z`:
  counterclockwise, seen from above. `pivot` is the point that `rot`
  turns about.
- The JSON key `in` (the `inside=` argument of the
  [`body`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#body) builder)
  puts a body in another body. The inner body moves and turns with it. A
  `group` body has no shape and only holds other bodies.
- [`body`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#body) kinds
  and their `size`: `box` `[x, y, z]`, `cylinder` `[radius, height]` or
  `[top radius, bottom radius, height]`, `cone` and `capsule`
  `[radius, height]`, `sphere` `[radius]`, `torus` `[radius, tube]`.
  `color` is one of `body light dark glass acc ok no`.
- `force(dir, mag)` is an arrow. `dir` is a direction in the world, and
  each item can be a state key. `mag` is a number or a key, and a
  negative `mag` turns the arrow round. `on` and `at` fix its start.
  `tone` is one of `up down side acc ok no ink`.
- [`label3d`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#label3d) is
  a chip of at most 60 characters on a body (`on`) or a point (`at`).
  The scene places the chips so that they do not overlap.
- [`shot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#shot) names a
  camera: `wide`, `side`, `front`, `top` or `close:<body id>`. A
  [`choice`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#choice) and
  a [`shot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#shot) with
  the same `bind` key give the learner a camera picker.
- Compute a direction with trigonometry in `derive`, then put the
  derived keys in `dir`. Say in the scene `label` when sizes and
  distances are not to scale.

source is the `md(spec)` fence draws the demo. `page(spec)` gives the
HTML as a string. `theme='paper'` gives the paper look.

## Check in a browser

`from rupaka.check import check, can_check`. `check(spec)` draws the
demo in headless Chromium and plays it. It gives
`AttrDict(ok, errors, info, shots)`. It finds errors that
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
cannot see: a script error, a network request, a gate that shows its
answer, a control that keys do not move, and text with low contrast.

[`check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#check) needs
the [`check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#check)
extra (`rupaka[check]`) and playwright’s Chromium
(`python -m playwright install chromium`), or a browser in
`$FASTCDP_CHROME`.
[`can_check()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#can_check)
is True when both are there.
[`check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#check) never
starts the everyday Chrome.

## Ask a model for a demo

`author(concept, ask)` in `rupaka.agent` asks a model for a demo, then
validates it, plays it in a headless browser and repairs it.
`ask(prompt, sp)` is any function that sends a prompt and a system
prompt to a model and gives back text.
[`author`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/agent.html#author) gives
the best spec that passed
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
and [`check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#check), or
None. Its texts can still fail
[`plain_errors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#plain_errors),
so run
[`plain_errors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#plain_errors)
on the result.

When you are the model, read
[`catalog()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/agent.html#catalog),
write the spec, and run
[`validate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#validate)
and
[`plain_errors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#plain_errors)
until both give `[]`. `near(dict(name=..., statement=..., subject=...))`
gives the two gallery demos that share the most words with a concept. In
`rupaka.spec`,
[`gallery()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#gallery)
gives every gallery demo by id, and
[`examples()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/spec.html#examples)
gives the example spec of each block.

## Boards and room questions

A board is the screen guide’s answer: one spoken line for each step,
marks on the page, and a side panel. A model writes it as JSON lines in
a closed language (`rupaka.board.OPS`). `clean_context(raw)` keeps the
known keys of the page context. `parse_board(text, ctx)` checks each
line against that context and drops a bad line.
`stream_board(chunks, ctx, on_step)` reads a reply as it comes and gives
the whole checked board at the end. When the header’s `sure` is `SURE`
(0.7) or more, `on_step(step, k)` gets each step when its first mark is
in, and again each time its strokes change.

`rupaka.poll.of_gate(spec, gate)` makes a question for a room from a
gate, with the index of the answer. `public(question)` removes the
answer and the source.

## This sheet in a harness

The `pyskills` entry point `rupaka` names this module. Leela and
ramabana list it with the other skills, and `read_skill('rupaka')` reads
it. When `pyskills` is installed, this module allows the names in
`ALLOW` in a sandbox.
[`save`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/render.html#save) and
[`check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#check) are not
in `ALLOW`, because they write a file and start a browser. Call them
yourself.

`mv_skill_md(dry_run=False)` writes this sheet as
`.agents/skills/rupaka/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/rupaka/SKILL.md` in
the current git repository, for Claude Code, Codex and other harnesses
that read Agent Skills.

## The hook

The Markdown cells above are the docstring of `rupaka.skill`. `pyskills`
reads the docstring without an import, and takes its first paragraph as
the summary.

`ALLOW` lists the functions that a sandboxed agent may call: the
builders, the checks that only read, and the functions that give text.
`pyskills` is not a dependency of rupaka, so the hook runs only when it
is installed.

## The SKILL.md

[`skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/skill.html#skill_md)
gives the same text as an Agent Skills `SKILL.md`: a front matter with
`name` and `description`, then the body. The description is a JSON
string, which YAML reads as a quoted text, so a colon in it is safe.

## Tests

Each name in `ALLOW` is a real function. `allow` skips a missing name
and says nothing, so this test catches a rename.

``` python
from rupaka.skill import ALLOW
for m, ns in ALLOW.items():
    for n in ns: assert callable(getattr(m, n, None)), f'{m.__name__}.{n}'
```

The first example of the sheet runs, and its spec is good.

``` python
import rupaka.skill as sk
ex = sk.__doc__.split('```python\n', 1)[1].split('```', 1)[0]
exec(ex, ns := {})
assert validate(ns['d']) == [] and ns['fence'].startswith('```rupaka')
```

The front matter has the name and a one-line description. The `SKILL.md`
copies in this repository match the sheet. After an edit to the sheet,
run `mv_skill_md(dry_run=False)` and commit the copies.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
from fastcore.xtras import find_file_parents
md_text = sk.skill_md()
head, body = md_text.split('\n---\n', 1)
assert head.startswith('---\nname: rupaka\ndescription: "Make interactive teaching demos')
assert body.lstrip().startswith('## Make a demo')
root = find_file_parents('.git')
for d in ('.agents', '.claude'): test_eq((root/d/'skills/rupaka/SKILL.md').read_text(), md_text)
```
